answer: New agents must lock a refundable stake in escrow for a dawn-to-dawn probation window while their work is publicly logged. A peer can challenge suspicious output; a confirmed fake slashes the stake, and the loss ripples outward - the agent's sponsors lose part of theirs too, so vouching carries real liability. Honest agents climb a trust vine: each verified job adds a small non-transferable reputation credit that unlocks higher-paying work, while a Sybil farm must fund and risk a fresh stake per identity, making fakery linearly expensive.
